title: Crystal Palace’s Jean-Philippe Mateta ‘back’ for Conference League tie vs. Larnaca
content:
Crystal Palace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta will return to the squad for their UEFA Conference League round-of-16 tie with AEK Larnaca on Thursday after managing a knee injury.

Mateta has been absent with the knee problem since the 3-1 defeat by Chelsea in the Premier League on January 25, but it has been ongoing since November last year.

The 28-year-old saw a January move to AC Milan collapse partly due to the injury, with some Palace supporters unhappy with his decision to reject a new contract and potentially move, although manager Oliver Glasner said he had not handed in a formal transfer request.

Together with the club, it was decided that he would not undergo surgery after consulting knee specialists and instead it would be managed through a period of rest.

“JP is back (to face Larnaca),” Glasner said in his press conference on Wednesday. “He started to train with us on Monday this week and will be in the squad as well. Everything goes in the right direction.”

However, he clarified that the French forward will not be ready to start and is likely to settle for a place on the bench.

“No (he can’t play the full game). He didn’t train for five or six weeks on the pitch,” Glasner continued. “He has been back for three days so there is no chance. He showed in training that he is always able to create chances to score goals that’s why it’s good to have him back.

“It was the target of winter window was to strengthen our attack because very often we were short of numbers. The club did a great job to strengthen our attack. It gives us more options if we need.”

Mateta has scored just once in his past 12 appearances in all competitions but is Palace’s second highest goalscorer with eight goals, all of which have come in the Premier League. He was guilty of missing two good chances against Larnaca in the 1-0 defeat during the initial league phase of the Conference League.

“I know if JP stays, he will be highly motivated because he has a big dream to play for France at the World Cup and therefore he needs to perform; he needs to play better than he played in the past couple of weeks,” Glasner said in his press conference before the 1-1 draw with Nottingham Forest on February 1. “He needs to score goals.”

It remains to be seen what sort of reception he will receive, with songs critical of Mateta coming from the away end during that draw with Forest and the unhappiness over the noise surrounding his future in January seemingly continuing to rankle among some fans.

Meanwhile, Daniel Munoz is not expected to miss a significant period with a shoulder injury suffered in the 3-1 win over Tottenham Hotspur on Thursday, and while he will miss the tie with Larnaca, he could return to face Leeds United in the Premier League on Sunday.

“Maxence (Lacroix) is back and can play tomorrow,” Glasner added, while saying he would consider playing a winger at wing-back. “Jeff Lerma was in squad but we could rest him at Tottenham. He’s fine.

“It’s just Daniel Munoz will miss this game and he’s working very hard together with our medical staff to be available for the Leeds game, but it’s still questionable. All others are in good shape.”
